# Wangala Festival 2026: Garo 100 Drums Festival, Meghalaya, Guinness Record and UPSC Notes


Wangala Festival (100 Drums Festival) of the Garo tribe, Meghalaya: golden jubilee, 1,000 drummers and Guinness World Record, with UPSC notes.


Festivals


Nov, 2026


•


4 min read


### Overview


The 50th, or golden jubilee, edition of the Wangala Festival of the Garo community of Meghalaya ran from 11 to 14 November 2026 at Chibragre near Tura. On 14 November, 1,000 drummers performed and the event entered the Guinness World Records (The Hindu, 14 Nov 2026).


## Why in the News: Wangala Golden Jubilee and Guinness World Record


The 50th edition of the Wangala Festival ran from 11 to 14 November 2026 at the Garo Heritage Village (Wangala A'dam), Chibragre, near Tura.


- On 14 November, 1,000 drummers performed and the event entered the Guinness World Records.
- Union Culture and Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat and Meghalaya Chief Minister Conrad K Sangma attended the concluding ceremony.
- The festival had more than 300 stalls.

## What Is Wangala? The 100 Drums Festival


Wangala is the harvest festival of the Garo community. It is also called the 100 Drums Festival.


- It honours Saljong, the Sun god.
- It marks the end of the farming season and the onset of winter.
- The drum is called the *dama* and is nearly 4 feet long.


## From a Small Tradition to a Formal Festival: 1976 to 2026


Wangala began as a small tradition with fewer than 10 drummers. It was given formal shape in 1976 at Chandmary Field, Tura, when a Block Development Officer gathered 10 dama players. The 2026 edition was the 50th, the golden jubilee (The Hindu, 14 Nov 2026).

## Reported Figures and a Discrepancy on Dancer Numbers


Outlets report the numbers differently. All of them agree that 1,000 drummers performed on 14 November 2026.


- The Hindu reports 1,500 dancers.
- Other outlets report 3,000 dancers.


Aspirants should not rely on a single dancer figure, and the drummer figure of 1,000 is the one to use for the Guinness record.


## Prelims Note: Garo Community and Meghalaya


The Garo are a community of Meghalaya, in north-east India. Wangala is associated with the Garo community and with the Tura area. For Prelims, remember the festival, the god it honours (Saljong, the Sun god), the instrument (dama) and the place (Tura and Chibragre).

## Key Takeaways


- Wangala is the harvest festival of the Garo community, also called the 100 Drums Festival.
- It honours Saljong, the Sun god, and marks the end of the farming season and the onset of winter.
- The drum is the dama, nearly 4 feet long.
- It was given formal shape in 1976 at Chandmary Field, Tura.
- The 50th edition ran from 11 to 14 November 2026 at Chibragre, and 1,000 drummers entered the Guinness World Records on 14 November.
- Dancer numbers are reported as 1,500 (The Hindu) and 3,000 (other outlets).
